summary.prose: This Story lets a terminal UI user set a tier to the Claude tool on an Ollama model from the Model Tiers screen. The Ollama runner already appears in the runner cycle because the screen lists every family the daemon declares; this Story labels each of its models cloud or local, keeps the 'type another model id' path away from it, and shows a tier whose model the definitions no longer declare as 'not supported, the tier will not run' instead of the vendor message that it runs a default. Everything comes from the daemon's definitions answer; the screen recognises the family by its host mark, never by name.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Model the new runner as a new family in the model definitions (alternative a1). The definitions file, its validator and the definitions answer gain one family, 'ollama-claude', with the CLI kind 'claude' and a host mark 'ollama'; every model of that family carries a hosting mark, 'cloud' or 'local'. Tier settings, effort filtering and provider construction keep their one per-family path. A family with the Ollama host mark builds the existing CLI provider with an Ollama target applied to that subprocess only, and clients use the host mark to show cloud/local and to never offer unlisted model ids for that family. Scope change 2026-10-29 (user decision): the Codex-on-Ollama family is withdrawn, because Ollama's cloud models ignore a requested output format and the Codex tool depends on it (DEF non-goal, citation c9 of the DEF).

consumedContracts.name: Ollama-hosted CLI families in the definitions answer
consumedContracts.purpose: The wire shape every consumer reads to know the new family, that it runs a CLI on Ollama, and which of its models are cloud or local.

consumedContracts.name: Tier resolution on an Ollama-hosted family
consumedContracts.purpose: How the daemon reports the tier it actually runs when the tier names a host family, including a model the definitions do not declare, so the run layer and every settings surface show the same outcome.

boundary.internal: The terminal UI's runner list, model list with cloud/local labels, effort step and the withheld 'enter another id' path for host families, and its display of the resolved tier, stay inside s3.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The shipped definitions entry for the new family and its models (which cloud and local models are supported), the catalog validator's four-member check and the 'hosting required on host families' rule, the registry's mapping from a CLI client to its direct family only, and the refusal of the unknown-model check and the approved-model store for host families stay inside s1.

How the CLI provider points a run at Ollama (the claude environment, applied only to that subprocess), the pre-run checks that Ollama answers and the model is available or signed in for a cloud model, the failure messages that name the cause, and the time limit that keeps a run from waiting forever stay inside s2.

The VS Code tier picker's family and model steps, the settings write validation that refuses an undeclared model for a host family, the cloud/local labels and the withheld 'enter another id' item stay inside s4.
The JetBrains Settings page's family and model selectors, the cloud/local labels, the filter that keeps host families out of the model-check flow, and its display of the resolved tier stay inside s5.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — run on Ollama and expose in settings

nonFunctional.performance: No added cost on today's runners. A run on a host family adds one Ollama reachability and model-availability check before the CLI starts; a run never waits beyond the existing CLI time limit.
nonFunctional.security: The Ollama settings are applied only to the started subprocess's environment or arguments; the user's own CLI configuration files and the daemon's environment are never changed. No API key is stored; the claude CLI gets the placeholder token Ollama accepts locally.
nonFunctional.observability: The daemon logs the family, model, hosting and Ollama target of each host-family run, and a failed pre-run check logs which check failed; the tier resolution reported to clients names a 'model-not-supported' fallback.
nonFunctional.durability: Nothing new is persisted: tier settings keep their stored shape, and the new families live in the shipped definitions file.

api.signature: function computeEffectiveTiers(tiering: AnalyzeTiering, defs: ModelDefinitionsResult): EffectiveTiers  // EffectiveTier gains: readonly hosting?: 'cloud' | 'local'; readonly notSupported: boolean

parameters.name: defs
parameters.purpose: The daemon's definitions answer, now read for each family's host and each model's hosting.

returns.meaning: As today, and each tier also carries `hosting` when its family has a host and serves the model, and `notSupported: true` when its family has a host and does not serve the configured model (served stays false). A vendor family's unserved model keeps notSupported false.

api.name: ModelTiersPane

returns.meaning: The Model Tiers screen. For a tier on a family with a host: the row shows the model followed by its hosting ('cloud' or 'local'); when notSupported it shows 'not supported by <family displayName>: the tier will not run; pick a listed model with m' instead of the vendor 'not served' note; the 'n' key hint is hidden and 'n' does nothing; 'e' on a model with no efforts toasts 'this model takes no effort setting'; 'e' on a notSupported tier toasts '<model> is not supported by <family>: pick a listed model with m' (the vendor 'pick one with m, or check it with n' toast at ModelTiersPane.tsx:184 stays for vendor families only). Other families render and behave as today.

Each edit still writes the whole tier object with one config.write.

dataModelChanges.details: Adds hosting?: 'cloud' | 'local' (a host family's served model) and notSupported: boolean (a host family not serving the configured model, mirroring the daemon's 'model-not-supported' resolution). served keeps its meaning.

+ readonly hosting?: 'cloud' | 'local' | undefined;
+ readonly notSupported: boolean;

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Reads `host` on a family and `hosting` on a model from the definitions answer (svc.models.definitions) to label models cloud/local and to recognise a family whose models are a closed list; the family is never named by id in src/cli.

Mirrors the daemon's tier resolution for a host family: a declared model runs as configured (an unlisted effort is shown as dropped, as today), an undeclared model resolves to 'model-not-supported' and is shown as not supported and not run, with no substitute shown.

errorCases.scenario: A tier is configured (hand-edited config, or a model removed in a later release) on the Ollama-hosted family with a model the definitions do not declare.
errorCases.detection: computeEffectiveTiers finds the family has a host and servedModel returns undefined for the configured model, so it sets notSupported true.
errorCases.response: The tier row shows the configured model and 'not supported by <family>: the tier will not run; pick a listed model with m'; 'e' toasts '<model> is not supported by <family>: pick a listed model with m' (not the vendor 'check it with n' message, since 'n' is withheld for a host family).
errorCases.userImpact: The user sees the tier will not run (matching the daemon's 'model-not-supported' refusal) and fixes it with 'm', instead of being told it runs a default.

errorCases.scenario: The user presses 'n' on a tier whose family has a host, or types an unlisted id into a prompt opened before switching family.
errorCases.detection: The pane hides and ignores 'n' when the tier's family has a host; resolveTypedModel returns refused for a host family's unserved id.
errorCases.response: No prompt opens; a typed unlisted id is refused with 'only listed <family> models are selectable' and nothing is written or checked.
errorCases.userImpact: The user can only pick a declared model; the unknown-model check is never offered for the Ollama runner.

errorCases.scenario: The daemon is down or an older daemon answers the definitions without host or hosting.
errorCases.detection: svc.models.definitions rejects (existing daemonProblem path), or the family entry has no host field.
errorCases.response: Daemon down: the existing 'the daemon is not running' message. No host field: the family is treated as today's families (no labels, no refusal), so an older daemon behaves as before.
errorCases.userImpact: No new failure mode; labels and refusals appear once the daemon is s1 or later.

alternativesConsidered.name: Host-aware pane logic over the definitions answer
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the pane's one data path (definitions + config): model-tiers.ts learns the host mark, so the tier row labels cloud/local, the typed-id path refuses a host family, and an undeclared host model is shown as 'not supported, will not run'.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
In src/cli/panes/model-tiers.ts, EffectiveTier gains the host-family status (served, unserved for a vendor family, or not supported for a host family) derived from the family's host mark in the definitions answer, and `hosting` for a served host model. resolveTypedModel refuses a typed id that a host family does not serve ('only listed <displayName> models are selectable'), so the unknown-model check screen is never opened for it. effortChoices is unchanged (it already offers only the model's own efforts plus the CLI default).

In ModelTiersPane.tsx the tier row appends the model's hosting ('cloud' / 'local') for a host family, replaces the 'not served: runs the default until approved' note with 'not supported by <family>: the tier will not run; pick a listed model with m' when the model is not supported, the 'e' key says 'this model takes no effort setting' when the model lists none, and the 'n' key hint and prompt are withheld for a host family. Families are recognised by `host`, never by id, so the literal scan stays green. 'f' already offers every family, so ollama-claude appears next to today's runners; switching to it picks the family's first declared model (familyDefaultTier's existing fallback).
pros: Smallest change: one pure module and one pane, the pane's existing data path and tests reused.
Shows the same outcome the daemon applies (sc2) using the host mark the definitions answer already carries (sc1).
No new IPC or daemon change; s4 and s5 are untouched.
cons: The pane mirrors the daemon's rule rather than asking the daemon, so a future change to the rule must be made in both places (the same trade-off the existing 'served' flag already makes).

alternativesConsidered.name: Ask the daemon for each tier's resolution
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add a models.resolveTier IPC returning the daemon's TierResolution per tier, and have the pane show that instead of computing it.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new daemon handler (next to models.resolveRole in src/daemon/model-definitions.ts) returns resolveTierWith's TierResolution for core/mid/cheap, including fallback 'model-not-supported'. The TUI's model service gains resolveTier, and the pane renders family/model/effort and the fallback from it, while the editing keys work as in a1 (cloud/local labels, refused typed ids for host families).
pros: The displayed tier is exactly what the daemon computes, with no mirrored rule.
cons: Adds a daemon IPC method, which s3's boundary does not own and every client (VS Code, JetBrains) would be expected to adopt; an HLD amendment would be needed.
One more round trip per pane load and a new failure mode (an older daemon without the method).
The editing keys still need a1's host-aware logic, so it is a1 plus an IPC.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Equal on ac1-ac3 but partial on sc2 (a new daemon IPC outside s3's boundary) and strictly more work, since it still needs a1's editing logic.
